 Day Full Video: Ohio State coach on Fahey ‘We've got to do a better job around him’
 Ohio State coach Ryan Day met with the media at noon today. He was asked about issues that arose in the loss at USC and what needs to happen as the team prepares to face Oregon.
 Steve Helwagen 45 
 We have video of Ohio State coach Ryan Day's weekly press conference held earlier today at the Woody Hayes Athletic Center.
 Media members peppered Day for about a half hour on questions of what wrong in the Buckeyes' 30-18 loss at USC this past Saturday. They also asked about this Saturday's matchup with Oregon (3:30 p.m., CBS).
 Below, we have the video as well as excerpts of Day's comments.
 SPEEDING UP 
 * On the slow tempo of the offense when OSU trailed in the fourth quarter -- "I mean, we did speed it up. I mean, I think we probably could have gone faster, but looking back, it was at 13 plays and so we ended up kind of taking some underneath stuff, and then as we got closer down in there, it took us a while to, like, score. You know, I think we, I think we ate up a couple minutes there inside the 20-yard line.
 "Up until then, I thought we were moving it decent, but we did get bogged down a little bit once we got inside the 20-yard line and needed to move faster. So we were kind of sugar huddling in there, making sure everybody was on the same page and going, but we certainly would have wanted to move faster there."
 * On not using the quarterback sneak at the USC 1-yard line -- "Yeah, well, yeah, you can as you get closer in there. It's on the one-yard line. They're kind of submarineing in there, and you got to make a decision if you feel like you can move a guy submarine with a young quarterback on the half-yard line.
 "You know, on the one before, it's not gaps defense where guys are kind of in that we call root hog where they're knocking the guys back, and so we wanted to kind of put in the running backs hands in that spot, and we didn't get in. You know, we kept a couple of receivers on the field and got hit off the edge there, so, but at the end of the day, like we're still on the half-yard line and the penalty is really what set us back there, and that was completely unacceptable."
 * On how they put together a red zone plan -- "Well, I think when you go back through, you have to first off look at like anything, anytime you don't have success. It's the scheme, is it the personnel, or is it the coaching, and yeah, we can continue to go back through and see if there's schematically ways we can do better, which is exactly what we need to do. Ultimately, everything that happens on the field is my responsibility, so I'm involved with everything, but yeah, to say that it's working very well is not accurate.
 "You know, I think it's hard for anybody to score touchdowns in a red zone nowadays. I think when you see that across college football, it's getting harder and harder. I'm not making excuses, I'm just saying we have to execute cleanly down there, and when we have negative plays, and we have penalties, then it certainly sets us way back.
 "So when we get down in there, typically we're late into a drive, and I don't think we've done a very good job of sustaining drives. I think when you look at the way we've been 13, 11, 15 play drives, and then we're not finishing off the drives well enough when we get down in there.
 "In one play, whether it's a negative play on a, whatever it might be, a mis-execution or a penalty, it is setting us back. So we have to do a better job of focusing, making sure that it's simple and it's clean. Certainly have to be aggressive.
 "I think it's not like we're not throwing it down there, but then at the same time if we can create more explosives where we can score from further out too, then that would create some of the problems, but at the end of the day, once we get down to red zone, we have to be able to run the ball and then we have to be able to win on one-on-ones on the outside, and you know, certainly that is something that is extremely frustrating. So we've got to keep working at it this week, and I don't know what else to say other than that, but I'm as frustrated as anybody."
 VIDEO INTERVIEW: COACH DAY
 ANY STAFF CHANGES?
 * On whether he is considering coaching changes -- "I mean, yeah, I don't think that I'm like against any of that if it's appropriate. I don't, I'm not in that frame of mind right now, but at the same time, I think, again, going back to what we were talking about before, you have to identify, is it the personnel? So maybe we need to change and move some guys around.
 "I think it does hurt missing some guys, but I think at the end of the day, we feel like we have enough here to win these games. Then you look at scheme, and when I go back through the scheme, there are definitely some plays on both sides of the ball that I think schematically we can do better. There are, but it's not an overall, like, issue that we're like running bad plays or we're running bad defense.
 "I don't, I don't see that as a major problem. There's always things we can do better, certainly recognize that. To me, we have to coach it better.
 "We've got to coach it better, and again, that starts right here, but then it goes to the coordinators, and then it goes to position coaches, and so that's our job to make sure that we're coaching better, and now the players they have to hold themselves accountable too, and there's a certain level of accountability for these guys that they're expected to do their job at a high level, but that's the way that I'm approaching this week, is that we all have to coach this better and take responsibility as a player, and that's the way that I've evaluated coming out of the USC game."
 GOING AGAINST RAIOLA
 * On facing Oregon and former Ohio State commit Dylan Raiola at quarterback -- "Well, first off, they have as much talent as anybody in the country. This is, this team is excellent. I know that they've lost three games, but put the film on.
 "I mean, they have NFL players all over the field, and they have speed at wideout, they have a good offensive line, a really good tight end, the running backs run hard, and then Raiola has played a lot of football as an experienced quarterback, so this is a major challenge for us, and you saw the way that they played against USC, and we just lost the USC, so I know that maybe some of these records or whatever this season seem a little bit out of whack, but this team going into the season was predicted to be the national champ, and they haven't lost a whole bunch of players. They're really talented.
 "They're very, very good on defense as well. I mean, this is as good of a team as we've played all year in terms of talent, and when they're on, they're on, and they played really good last week, so and Dylan, in particular he's played a lot of football, and he has got a strong arm. He understands what's going on.
 "He's an older guy, so we talked about it before that the margin for error here is tiny, and so we better recognize that if we don't get these things fixed and play better, like, this isn't gonna get any better against Oregon. We've got to be better than they are in all phases, and so, yeah, I mean, that's the challenge for this week, and yeah, it's not gonna go well if we don't get these things fixed, like, now, and so the urgency had better be really high for everybody, coaches and players included."
 FIXING THE ISSUES
 * On diagnosing what needs fixed -- "No, again, all of a sudden, you don't just change everything, but you have to recognize what needs to change, and when you come out of a game like that there's just a lot of things that we need to get answered why these things happen, and as you can imagine having a freshman quarterback, there's a lot of my my time was with the quarterbacks and meetings and everything like that, so still, obviously, with the team, addressing the team meetings, addressing before the game one-off situations involved with all the special teams.
 "But we need everyone to step up, and that's the bottom line, and everyone needs to understand that, and so as the head coach, it's my job to make sure I'm direct in exactly what the expectations are and making sure everybody's being held accountable, and that starts right with me, then it goes to coordinators and down, right on down the list from everybody in the building, and that's, the expectations here, like we said, when we lost Julian, didn't change, so said it before, we're not allowed to lose games, and when that happens there's consequences, that's just the way it is, and if you don't like it, then don't come to Ohio State."
 THE SUNDAY MEETING
 * On how he approached the team on Sunday -- "No, you can't, you can't put on an act, I mean, you have to be who you are the minute you start doing that, and I've, one thing I try to take my, take a lot of pride in, is that I don't become some cartoon character and try to put on a show for people and be an actor. I try to be exactly who I am, exactly what's going on in that moment, and address the problems and be real, and that's what, that's what needs to happen."
 * On comments about a lack of effort on defense -- "I felt like there were some plays early in the game where that happened, I think as the game went on, we started playing much faster, but there was, there was missed tackles and giant plays, and, and that was the tail of the tape you look at the two massive 70 yarders, you look at the third and 19, you look at some of that stuff, it's completely unacceptable, so yeah, we all have to look in the mirror and figure out why exactly that happened, and it happens again this week, we're in trouble."
 MOVING FORWARD
 * On how the team moves forward after a loss -- "I think you got to challenge everybody challenge everybody in the building, challenge the, the older guys who have been here before not only got to have to do their job and lead, but they got to bring guys along with them, and they understand what has to happen and the consistency that has to happen throughout the season, and so they got to bring guys along with them."
 * More on the question of playing up tempo -- "Well, I think you've seen us mix it in, and it's there definitely been times where I think it's helped us, and so we have to identify whether it'll help us moving forward here each week, and we'll do that here against Oregon."
 MULTIPLE TIGHT END SETS
 * On using multiple tight end sets -- "Yeah, well, I think the reason you change up groupings is to attack the defense from a couple different surfaces, so as you know, when you have one tight end in the game, it's a three-surface side, three receivers in the game, when you have multiple tight ends, there's ways to get to four surfaces or three surfaces on both sides, which changes the personnel, which changes the fits, changes the stress on the defense, so the ability to go in and out of groupings can really be a positive.
 "I think the tight ends have been solid as a group, but we always have to evaluate and be real and figure out, like, what is the give and take on all that, and I still think that there's a lot of value to what we're doing in terms of having them in the game, but we'll keep evaluating it this week, and we can't be slamming our head against the wall, either."
 * On how the wide receiver group has performed -- "There's a long conversation I have about that schematically that I don't think I really want to get into right now, but whether it's quarterback run, quarterback reading somebody, RPO, there's just a lot that goes into that conversation that we all talk long and hard about to figure out what the identity is going to be at the beginning of the season, and then we try to build it from there, but I do hear what you're saying, and that's all part of the conversation."
 FAHEY'S PERFORMANCE
 * On how Luke Fahey played in his first start at quarterback -- "Well, I think, like we said going into it, we all got to help this guy out, and I don't think we did. I thought he had the right approach. It was not all perfect.
 "There were certainly things that happened operationally that for a young quarterback, it was a lot on him, and he was working through it. You know, there were some misthrows, but we expected all that to happen. He also made a lot of plays.
 "He also had command of the huddle. He also showed some grit out there and toughness, and so I go to the players the offensive line, I go to the wide receivers, and just say, man, what was it like in there? And, I mean, they were very positive about his approach out there, and I think you saw him extend some plays.
 "I thought you saw him make some plays. He kept playing all the way to the end. I thought his attitude was good on the sideline, even though we couldn't quite get in at some of these red zone opportunities.
 "So, there's things to build on there, for sure, but we've got to do a better job around him, helping him out as a young player."
 * On whether Fahey will start vs. Oregon -- "Yeah, right now. Yeah, he's going to start against Oregon."
 BOWEN AS O-LINE COACH
 * On Tyler Bowen's performance as the O-line coach – "Right, well, it's something that you've got to evaluate everybody, and that's the thing about being at Ohio State. You know, the expectations are very high. You know, I think that there's definitely some positive things that have gone on there, but when you come out of the last game or two, I think that there's just been too many mistakes there, and so we have to improve on that, and I think he would tell you that he's working as hard as he can to get those things fixed and try to figure out ways to put these guys in better situations and coach them better, and that's the bottom line. So, well, we know what needs to get done, and we've had too many penalties, had too many missed assignments, and I think everybody in that group room would tell you that.
 "There's no, like, guys skirting around any of that, and I think he would tell you the same thing. So, he's going to get back to work, and we all know what the expectation is."
 * On special teams penalties – "We have to clean them up. Yeah, no, it's not is what it is.
 "There's nothing that is what it is. We've got to get it fixed. The holding play on Miles was a play where he was kind of getting knocked back, and he grabbed the back of his pads.
 "He can't do that, and that's based on technique. Beau's penalty on the sideline, that's the second time that's happened. When we get near there, I think it was close.
 "We turned it in. I'm not going to get into that conversation, but still, we can't leave it to be close. Those are big-time decisions, 15 yards.
 "And then the delay of game, that's on coaching. We got the thing in late. We made a check, and instead of taking a timeout in that situation, we decided to take a delay of game.
 "I didn't want to lose a timeout. And as much as I don't want to lose five yards, I also don't want to lose a timeout or get the thing blocked. So one of them was coaching, and then the two other, one was the technique, and then the other one was controlling the emotion.
 "So what is the common thread? It's because to me, the penalties are killer. And I got to tell you, at the end of the day as a coach, you got to look yourself in the mirror and figure out why that's happening.
 "So if there are guys that it's continually happening, we got to make a change. And then holding guys accountable in practice the best we possibly can and teaching better technique."
 MODELING AFTER NFL
 * On modeling the program after the NFL – "I mean, when you have a bad game and you lose, when you have two losses, you have to look at everything. And you can, trust me, I'm looking at everything to make sure that we're doing this the right way. Because to go into that game and play the way we did is not what I expected at all.
 "And so, yeah, I think the term NFL, I don't know, it's a pretty general statement, but we got to look at everything."
 * On what the best O-line alignment looks like – "Yeah, no, you can make them. And we'll see how the health shakes out this week, and then try to put the best five out there. Because part of that at this time of year is that we had Phil that was out, then we had Austin that was out.
 "So the good news is we do have some versatility there. But like you said, we got to find the right five that's available this week, and that's what we're gonna do. So yeah, you can move some guys cuz they've done it before.
 "But, and a lot of these guys have experience. So this is not like this is new."
 * On whether Austin Siereveld will be at left tackle – "It was depending on the week, how things go, but it wasn't a performance issue."
 FINDING THE BEST FIVE
 * On finding the best five on the OL – "Well, I think I know where they belong for the most part. When we had the injury, we moved Austin over and moved in Gabe. And then when Austin went out, Phil went in.
 "So that sort of took care of itself. We'll see how this week goes. But yeah, there was a point there, I think, maybe in the Iowa week, where we were moving pretty good.
 "And then the Indiana game, we had too many issues going on in protection. I thought we blocked them pretty good in the run game against Indiana. There was some really good runs in there for the most part.
 "I actually don't think that we hit some of the holes great, going back to that game. But this game right here, and you saw the explosive runs. We ran for, I think it was like 220 yards, and we had some sacks and things.
 "So it wasn't like we weren't blocking them there. But when it gets down into the red zone, we need it the most. And then in protection, to me, is where things have broken down.
 "And so that's where we've gotta be better. And the only way to do that is get back to work. So it's not completely broken here. It's just we've got to coach it better, and that's the way that I'm looking at it."
 FRUSTRATION FOR SMITH
 * On Jeremiah Smith showing frustration during the loss – "He's unbelievable. Like, he wants to win. And when he doesn't win, he gets frustrated. It's not about I need touches. Now, he also knows that when he touches the ball, good things happen. He wants to have an impact on the game.
 "He also knows sometimes when there's three guys covering him or whatever they do to take him away, the other guys need to step up. And so he's not pointing. He's not blaming fingers.
 "He just gets frustrated like we all do. And he's the ultimate competitor. But he's not somebody that's like saying give me the ball, I need the ball, although that's his mentality.
 "And so when there are opportunities to get him the ball and find ways to get him the ball, we have to do that, need to do that. And I think that's where Cortez, myself, and Arthur, going into the game plan, we'll try to explain to him, hey, here's our plan of attack. Here's how we're doing.
 "So we're all on the same page. So when we get in there, but hey, listen if there's double coverage here, it's going to be really hard for us. So here's what we need to do.
 "We need to run the ball over here. Or someone needs to step up in terms of a one-on-one situation. And that's the plan going in. So we're all on the same page. And then we just try to find ways, regardless of what they're doing, to get them the ball. And then you have to find out, are you trying to force that too much?
 "And then that's the balance that we try to find. But, no, when it comes to that, he's the ultimate competitor. He loves this team. He loves Ohio State. And he just hates to lose."
 THE PRESSURE TO WIN
 * On the importance to win every game – "I don't know. I think it's a hell of a question. But I would say, as time has gone on, I've just tried to do everything I can to win the game. And that's probably where I'll leave it."
 * On what happened when USC converted a third-and-19 with a running play – "No good. So there was the penalty on the play that was assessed. Call got changed and didn't get communicated.
 "And then so there was a misalignment. And that's all it takes. So again, the communication, the coaching, everybody involved. And that's all it takes. It just takes one guy to be out of a gap. And we're out of it.
 "And so that's a great example. And so these are the types of things that if we do them here again this week, then things aren't going to get any better. So we've got to get them fixed."
 * On DT Eddrick Houston's status after he limped off – "He's doing better. He's doing better. I think he plans to be out there today."
 HOW CLOSE IS THIS TEAM?
 * On how close the team is to being what it needs to be – "Well, I would have said going into the game, I thought we were very close. I didn't come out of the game feeling that way. Yeah.
 "Yeah, just being dead honest. The penalties are ridiculous. And the mistakes are ridiculous.
 "So ultimately, that leads me to believe that we're not where we need to be. So we've got an opportunity here against Oregon now to go turn that around. I think now is two hours away from our Tuesday meeting.
 "And we better get those things fixed. But if we're going to let that stuff linger around in here, it's going to affect our game against Oregon. And so I know we're debriefing here on last week's game.
 "But everybody in the Woody needs to come in here, learn the lessons from getting on the film Sunday, getting on the film a little bit yesterday. But it's on to Oregon. And so we've got to get those things fixed and feel the urgency of that, because this is a very, very good team.
 "And so now we've got these guys at home. And I think we have to have a great approach going into this week. And I think having the home crowd behind us is a big deal in this game.
 "Having that type of environment, one of the hostile environments that Ohio State's known for when these guys come in here. Because we need everybody. And when I talk about we need everybody to rally around the quarterback, that means the fans.
 "We have the greatest fans in the world. And so we need to give them something to cheer for. But we need them to be there for us. And I think all of that stuff needs to be the focus now. Because we can't sit here and dwell on what's gone on in the past. We better learn from it pretty damn quick, though."
 * On how the coaches will lean on Fahey in his second start – "That's the balance. That's the balance of trying to be aggressive, trying to give him enough that he can handle where we know that he doesn't have a lot of experience playing in these games and playing against a very good team. But also, we can't crawl up into a ball.
 "We got to go attack. And so I do think in that game, we did. There were a lot of opportunities there. And so we're gonna have to be the same way in this game. But that is the balance you try to strike as a coach when he's going into a second start ever."
